cacheKey.normalizedQuery: packages/main/src/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts:40-41: the mutant is written to <dirname(guardFile)>/__b49ed-mutant-<pid>.js, i.e. inside packages/main/dist/core/, which is also the tree hashed by scripts/full-suite-build-binding.mjs:verifyBuildBinding (every readFileSync/readdirSync under dist folds into distDigest). Reproduced directly: touching a stray file in dist/core while the manifest exists makes verifyBuildBinding throw stale full-suite dist: source/dist build binding mismatch (confirmed via node --input-type=module against the real worktree dist). verifyBuildBinding runs unconditionally at the top of scripts/build-main-with-binding.mjs on every npm run build invocation (the fast path used by the pre-push hook and CLAUDE.md build discipline). So any process that runs npm run build (or re-verifies the binding) while this smoke test's mutant file transiently exists between writeFileSync and the finally rmSync will see a spurious stale-dist failure and force an unnecessary rebuild under the build lock -- a real, demonstrated concurrency hazard, not just cosmetic residue. Using a tmpdir-based scratch path (as the file's own now-dead mkdtempSync scratch var originally implied) with a same-directory symlink, or writing outside dist entirely and resolving relative imports another way, would avoid touching the hashed tree at all. Crash-safety is fine (dist is gitignored and the atomic dist.staging/dist.trash swap discards orphans on next build), but the live concurrent-verify race is real. Correct, and the reviewer demonstrated it rather than asserting it: scripts/full-suite-build-binding.mjs hashes every file under packages/main/dist and verifyBuildBinding runs unconditionally at the top of npm run build, so a transient extra file in dist/core races with any concurrent build and throws 'stale full-suite dist'. I confirmed both the hashing behaviour and the throw site. Fixed by moving the mutant out of the hashed tree entirely: it now goes to a mkdtemp scratch dir outside the repo, and the guard's two relative imports (./authority-signing.js, ./digest.js) are rewritten to absolute file:// URLs so they still resolve from there. Added an assertion that no relative import survives the rewrite, so if a future import is added to the guard the relocation fails loudly instead of silently loading a different module. Verified: no __b49ed-mutant-* file remains under dist after a run, and the proof still bites (widening SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES exits 1, restoring exits 0).

devMemory.summary: A test's generic top-level assertion failure message can mask the REAL underlying cause -- don't trust a surface error message as the root cause without tracing what actually happened first, especially when triaging a test as 'unrelated pre-existing' to justify not fixing it.
devMemory.lesson: When a test fails with a message that sounds infrastructure/environment-related ('shim fired', 'marker never created', 'injection did not run'), and you're tempted to conclude 'unrelated, pre-existing, out of scope' -- verify by tracing the ACTUAL execution path (add temporary debug logging, or read the CLI's real stdout/stderr before the fixture's own assertion wrapper summarizes it), not just by checking 'is this file in my diff'. A file being untouched by your diff does NOT mean your diff didn't break it -- a new gate/check anywhere in the shared call path the file exercises can block it before it ever reaches the logic its own assertions describe. This is the same root-cause class as F-008 (a new gate running before pre-existing code the test expects to reach), just with a MORE misleading surface symptom this time.
devMemory.reusePrompt: test failure message sounds like infrastructure/environment / tempted to call it unrelated pre-existing / spawn_task for a test failure / verify root cause before triaging as out of scope / shim fired marker never created

devMemory.summary: Rerouting a lock/path argument at a call site can be a no-op if the callee already independently re-derives the same shared root internally.
devMemory.lesson: acquireStoryTransitionLock(root, storyId) looked like it needed a stable-root reroute to survive a winning DONE deleting the worktree it was called from -- but storyTransitionLockPath already resolves root through resolveSharedLockRoot (git-common-dir based, B-d877 R2 FIX B) BEFORE touching disk, so ANY root string passed in (worktree path or main repo root) resolves to the identical shared lock directory. The reroute compiled, built, and even made the target smoke test pass -- because the REAL fix (a separate StoryArtifactMissingError translation) was landed in the same commit, masking that the reroute itself did nothing. A REVIEW reviewer caught it by comparing storyTransitionLockPath(worktreePath, id) vs storyTransitionLockPath(mainRepoRoot, id) directly and finding them identical. Before adding a 'fix' that reroutes an argument into a shared/lock/root-resolution function, read the CALLEE's own resolution logic first -- if it already normalizes via git-common-dir or similar, the caller-side reroute is redundant. When a test passes after a multi-part fix, that does not mean every part of the fix is load-bearing; isolate and re-test each part before crediting it as the actual fix.
devMemory.reusePrompt: adding a stable-root/shared-root reroute before a lock or path helper / lock directory disappears with worktree teardown / fix passes tests but reviewer says a change is a no-op / multi-part fix, unclear which part is load-bearing

devMemory.summary: A new lifecycle-gate artifact written OUTSIDE .lattice/story/actives/<storyId>/ needs its own runtime-artifact-registry entry (materialHash:'exclude') -- autoCommitStoryMetadata never reaches it, and auto-committing the write directly is the wrong fix (moves HEAD, breaks other signed evidence freshness).
devMemory.lesson: First instinct was to auto-commit the write inside the handler (mirroring finding_resolve's commitHint/autoCommitStoryMetadata pattern) -- this worked for the immediate symptom but introduced a WORSE regression: the new commit moved HEAD, which retroactively invalidated any test-evidence.json/delivery-check.json already signed against the prior HEAD (stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch), confirmed via a targeted repro before landing. The correct fix is almost always to register the path in core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts (RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY) with materialHash:'exclude', which routes dirty-worktree classification to the non-blocking runtime_artifact_changes category via findRuntimeArtifactEntry, AND ensures the path never perturbs currentMaterialHash in the first place -- no commit-timing/HEAD-movement side effects at all. Only add ignorePatterns if the artifact should ALSO be gitignored; a deliberately git-tracked-but-non-authoritative artifact (like this one) should have ignorePatterns:[] so it stays visible/shareable while still being non-blocking.
devMemory.reusePrompt: review_run_start / dirty-worktree unexpected_dirty_files / new artifact outside story dir / stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch after auto-commit / RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY materialHash exclude
